summary: Master aviation statistical analysis and forecasting. Learn ICAO standards, ARIMA modeling, and fleet planning to drive airline and airport growth.
lede: Aviation Statistical Analysis and Forecasting Techniques shows you how to turn air transport data into evidence-based forecasts for demand, operations, and network performance. You will examine historical passenger and cargo traffic, distinguish seasonal patterns from structural shifts, and apply demand elasticity, load factor, fleet, airport throughput, and yield analysis. Using Box-Jenkins methodology, Holt-Winters exponential smoothing, multivariate regression, and risk-adjusted forecasting, you will build models grounded in Revenue Passenger Kilometers and Available Seat Kilometers data. Practical work with R, Python, traffic distribution models, break-even load factors, predictive dashboards, and route feasibility analysis prepares you to evaluate planning decisions under budgetary and regulatory constraints.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who manage, analyze, or report on aviation data to drive operational and strategic decisions.
modules: Aviation Data Ecosystem and ICAO Standards
Risk, Uncertainty, and Monte Carlo Simulation
AI and Machine Learning in Aviation Analytics
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of aviation operations and basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel. Prior experience with descriptive statistics (mean, median, standard deviation) is recommended. Access to a laptop with spreadsheet software is required for the duration of the course.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
